description:
From the 2026-08-19 gap audit of #152 vs ../foundationdb. Two holes, benign on the current branch only because shard/log families change solely in recovery's system transaction (whose content equals the unlock snapshot); both become real when the Distributor (q67.21) mutates shard_keys/ or layout mid-epoch:

1. Staleness race: finalize task N applies the window to RoutingData during resolution but sends {:routing_data_update} only after log push. A batch spawned in between snapshots metadata.version >= N (so the resolver will not re-send version N's entries) with a pre-N routing_data struct. The ETS shard table is immune (shared, mutated in place); log_map/log_services are per-struct - a layout_log change at version N is invisible to batch N+1's routing for the duration of batch N's log push. FDB prevents this with version-ordered stateMutations relay + shardChanged signaling (Resolver.actor.cpp:79-97).

2. No idempotence guard: Metadata.apply_updates is version-guarded; RoutingData.apply_mutations is not, and insert_log is non-idempotent (re-applied layout_log set appends a duplicate index). Overlapping windows to concurrent tasks are a documented protocol feature.

Fix shape: guarantee batch K+1 routes with all metadata <= K applied, and make RoutingData application version-guarded (e.g. fold log_map/log_services into the version-guarded server-side path, or route strictly from the in-task differential). Must land with or before q67.21's mid-epoch writer.
title: RoutingData window application: version-guard and ordering for mid-epoch shard-map churn
